periods.analysis: ERP Cloud Migration opened the reporting arc at 12% complete, with requirements and vendor selection complete and the project appropriately held at yellow. The primary control issue is that Finance module data migration remains in-progress even though that milestone is 10 days past its planned offset, so I am treating data quality and reconciliation as the gating risk. HR module cutover is not-started with 80 days of schedule runway, and legacy system decommission is not-started with 170 days of runway, which is acceptable only if the finance conversion stabilizes. The city’s financial position and AA bond rating give us room to execute carefully, but not room to let chart-of-accounts mapping or payroll interfaces drift.
periods.recommendations: Keep the project in yellow and require a weekly Finance Migration Control Log covering open conversion defects, owner, aging, and dollar exposure. Stand up a joint Finance-IT reconciliation lane for fund, department, project, and grant segments before expanding work into HR cutover tasks. Do not authorize any legacy decommission planning beyond inventory until the Finance module produces two clean trial balance extracts.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 12% to 16%, a 4-point quarter-over-quarter increase, which is steady but still below the pace I would prefer for a core finance system. Requirements and vendor selection remain complete, while Finance module data migration is still in-progress and still carries the 10-day overdue condition. HR module cutover remains not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission remains not-started with 170 days, so the downstream work is preserved but increasingly dependent on the quality of the finance data load. The yellow status is appropriate because we are advancing, but the risk is now less about vendor selection and more about conversion discipline across Harborview’s purchasing, utility billing, and capital project cost centers.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the weekly control log and add a formal data-conversion acceptance checklist signed by Finance, Budget, Purchasing, and IT Security. Direct the vendor team to run a second mock migration using the FY2024 close dataset, including encumbrances and open purchase orders from the waterfront facilities and public works divisions. Prepare the HR cutover workplan now, but hold execution until Finance migration exceptions are under the agreed tolerance.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 16% to 20%, another 4-point quarter-over-quarter gain, but it remains yellow because the Finance module data migration is still in-progress and 10 days past its planned offset. Requirements and vendor selection continue to be complete, which means governance should now focus on execution controls rather than procurement decisions. HR module cutover is still not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission is still not-started with 170 days, leaving a manageable but narrowing buffer. In practical terms, the unresolved items are the high-risk records: grant-funded capital projects, prior-year retainage, and vendor master duplicates.
periods.recommendations: Require a defect burn-down target by category, with separate reporting for chart-of-accounts, vendor master, open PO, and grant ledger defects. Assign Finance power users from Budget, Accounts Payable, Payroll, and Capital Accounting to validate 25-record samples each week against the legacy system. Keep HR cutover in planning mode only, and require a go/no-go control memo before any employee data is moved.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 20% to 24%, maintaining the same 4-point quarter-over-quarter movement and confirming that the project is progressing, but deliberately. The yellow rating remains justified because Finance module data migration is still in-progress and remains 10 days overdue, while requirements and vendor selection are complete. HR module cutover remains not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission remains not-started with 170 days, so we still have sequencing control if we do not consume the buffer informally. The city’s growth is increasing transaction volume, especially permits, utility payments, and capital invoices, which makes clean master data more important than hitting a cosmetic completion number.
periods.recommendations: Freeze nonessential changes to the chart of accounts and vendor master during the next mock conversion window. Have the project manager publish a two-week integrated schedule showing Finance migration tasks, HR readiness tasks, and decision points for legacy system dependencies. Add internal audit as an observer for migration evidence, not to slow the work, but to preserve confidence in controls and auditability.

periods.analysis: The project moved from 24% to 28%, again a 4-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the pattern is consistent: controlled progress with unresolved migration risk. Requirements and vendor selection remain complete, but Finance module data migration is still in-progress and still 10 days past due. HR module cutover and legacy system decommission remain not-started with 80 and 170 days of runway respectively, which keeps the overall sequence intact but creates pressure on testing windows. I am particularly watching interface controls for banking, utility billing, procurement cards, and budget transfers, because those are the areas where a clean implementation protects both operations and public trust.
periods.recommendations: Begin parallel-run planning for Finance, including daily cash, accounts payable, budget availability, and general ledger posting comparisons. Require the vendor to document interface control totals for the bank file, utility billing feed, and procurement card import before the next steering committee. Keep the status yellow until we have evidence of repeatable reconciliations, not just evidence that records can be loaded.

periods.analysis: Completion rose from 28% to 32%, preserving the 4-point quarter-over-quarter trend and showing that the project has not stalled. The concern is also unchanged: Finance module data migration remains in-progress and 10 days overdue, while requirements and vendor selection are complete. HR module cutover remains not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission remains not-started with 170 days, which is still defensible if Finance stabilization is near. Year-end adds a control burden because Harborview’s audit, budget development, and capital carryforward work all depend on reliable balances and clean supporting detail.
periods.recommendations: Use year-end close as a controlled validation event, with documented comparisons for fund balance, encumbrances, receivables, and capital project ledgers. Establish a January decision gate requiring Finance Director, IT, and project sponsor sign-off before HR cutover preparation moves from design to build. Keep legacy system decommission limited to application inventory, contract dates, and data-retention requirements until Finance has passed parallel-run thresholds.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 32% to 36%, another 4-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and remains in yellow because the core risk has not cleared. Requirements and vendor selection are complete, but Finance module data migration is still in-progress and remains 10 days past its planned offset. HR module cutover is still not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission is still not-started with 170 days, so the migration is still driving the entire critical path. At this stage, I view the key risk as conversion evidence: Harborview needs records that reconcile by fund, department, project, grant, and vendor, not verbal assurance that the system is close.
periods.recommendations: Require a formal migration evidence binder with control totals, exception reports, approvals, and remediation notes for each conversion cycle. Schedule a focused steering committee session on the Finance migration only, with no broader project presentation until the overdue milestone has a dated closure plan. Begin HR data profiling in a read-only sandbox so the team uses the 80-day runway productively without creating cutover risk.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 36% to 40%, continuing the same 4-point quarter-over-quarter movement and closing this eight-quarter view with measured progress rather than resolution. Requirements and vendor selection remain complete, while Finance module data migration is still in-progress and still 10 days overdue, so yellow remains the correct status. HR module cutover remains not-started with 80 days of runway, and legacy system decommission remains not-started with 170 days, preserving options but also confirming that the project is still in its controlled migration phase. The disciplined interpretation is that Harborview has avoided an uncontrolled cutover, but must now convert steady effort into closure of the Finance milestone.
periods.recommendations: Set a firm Finance migration closure date with named owners for remaining defects and require daily standups during the final conversion sprint. Approve HR cutover readiness work only for security roles, position-control mapping, and payroll interface design until Finance migration is formally accepted. Prepare a legacy decommission risk register now, including retention, read-only access, vendor notice periods, and audit retrieval requirements, so decommission can move quickly once the upstream controls are satisfied.

periods.analysis: 65% complete. 0 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: Requirements and vendor selection (due Dec 18, 2025).
periods.recommendations: Review the late milestones with the project owner and confirm recovery dates before the next reporting cycle.
